input: Which websites list both support orgs and shelter options for UMs across Dutch cities?
expected_output:
You can find information about both support organizations and shelter options for undocumented migrants (UMs) across Dutch cities on the following websites:

- Stichting LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties (support organizations) and https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang (shelters)
- Helpful Information by the Red Cross: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ (local organizations and shelter options)
context:
Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/|Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.|Q: When is somebody undocumented? A: An undocumented migrant is a person who has no right of residence in a country. They have no documents confirming a right of residence, such as a visa. Their work, residence or study visa has expired, or they may never have had one. 

They are mainly migrants who:
- have had their residence application rejected, for example asylum seekers whose application for asylum has been rejected;
- have not applied for a residence permit, either for regular residence or asylum;
- are victims of human trafficking;
- do not have a work permit, for example domestic workers.

EU citizens do not need to apply for a residence permit to be in the Netherlands legally. Migrants from the EU can therefore never be undocumented."
|Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.|Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/|Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang|Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).|Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.|Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.|Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

input: Explain what a Dublin claim is and why it restricts NL asylum seekers from local shelter programs.
expected_output: A Dublin claim means that an asylum seeker’s fingerprints have been registered in another EU country before arriving in the Netherlands. According to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, the first EU country where someone’s fingerprints are taken is responsible for processing their asylum application. Because of this, the Netherlands cannot process their asylum request, and the person must return to the first EU country. As a result, people with a Dublin claim are often not allowed to access local shelter programs in the Netherlands, as these programs are usually only for people whose asylum procedure is being handled in the Netherlands.

input: How do the vulnerabilities of undocumented migrants differ from those of EU citizens in the Netherlands?
expected_output: Undocumented migrants in the Netherlands are much more vulnerable than EU citizens because they do not have a residence permit and have very limited rights. They are not entitled to social benefits, cannot take out health insurance, and have only limited access to assistance and facilities from the government or other agencies. This makes them easy targets for exploitation and puts them at risk of unsafe or unhealthy situations. In contrast, EU citizens do not need a residence permit to be in the Netherlands legally and cannot be undocumented, so they have access to rights and services that undocumented migrants do not.

input: What criteria and steps must UM meet to access BBB/municipality shelters, considering Dublin claim restrictions?
expected_output:
To access BBB or municipality shelters, undocumented migrants (UM) must generally meet specific criteria: they usually need to have previously applied for asylum in the Netherlands. Importantly, people with a Dublin claim are often not eligible for these local shelter programs. 

The steps to access shelter are:
1. Contact a screening location or the BBB shelter directly to get information and share their situation.
2. The shelter will assess if the person meets the criteria (such as a previous asylum application and no active Dublin claim).
3. Admission is not guaranteed—shelters often have strict criteria and limited capacity.

Always check local possibilities first on https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang, and never send someone directly to a BBB without confirming eligibility with the local organization or TC.

input: How do BBB, LVV, and municipality shelters differ in access and criteria for UM in NL?
expected_output:
BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood), LVV (Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening), and municipality shelters all provide shelter for undocumented migrants (UM) in the Netherlands, but they differ in access and criteria:

- **BBB shelters**: Local shelters for UM, but access is limited. They often require that someone has a legal perspective on a new asylum request and may be full. People with a Dublin claim are usually not admitted. Always check criteria with the local organization before referring someone.

- **LVV shelters**: These were government/municipality programs for rejected asylum seekers, offering 24-hour shelter for up to 18 months, with professional guidance and support. Admission required a rejected asylum application. The national government will stop funding LVV from 2025, but some cities (Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven, Groningen) will continue the program.

- **Municipality shelters**: These are local programs, sometimes continuing the LVV model. Access and criteria vary by city, but generally, people must have previously applied for asylum. People with a Dublin claim are often excluded.

**Summary:**  
Access to all these shelters is restricted, with criteria such as a previous asylum application and no Dublin claim. Always check local requirements before referring someone. More information can be found on https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ and https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang.

input: How does an 18-month undocumented stay affect Dublin claimants’ asylum eligibility and shelter access?
expected_output:
An 18-month undocumented stay can affect Dublin claimants in two main ways:

1. **Asylum Eligibility:** If a person with a Dublin claim manages to stay in the Netherlands without being returned for 18 months, their Dublin claim expires. After this period, they can request asylum in the Netherlands, as the responsibility for their asylum procedure shifts from the first EU country to the Netherlands.

2. **Shelter Access:** During the 18 months, it is very hard for people with a Dublin claim to get support or shelter, as most local shelter programs do not accept Dublin claimants. Access to BBB or municipality shelters is usually denied to them until the Dublin claim expires. 

For more information, see: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang and https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/|Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.|Q: When is somebody undocumented? A: An undocumented migrant is a person who has no right of residence in a country. They have no documents confirming a right of residence, such as a visa. Their work, residence or study visa has expired, or they may never have had one. 

They are mainly migrants who:
- have had their residence application rejected, for example asylum seekers whose application for asylum has been rejected;
- have not applied for a residence permit, either for regular residence or asylum;
- are victims of human trafficking;
- do not have a work permit, for example domestic workers.

EU citizens do not need to apply for a residence permit to be in the Netherlands legally. Migrants from the EU can therefore never be undocumented."
|Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.|Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/|Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang|Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).|Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.|Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.|Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC.

input: How will LVV program funding and operations differ among Dutch cities after 2025?
expected_output: After 2025, the Dutch government will stop financing the LVV (Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening) program. As a result, the continuation of LVV shelters will depend on decisions made by individual cities. Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven, and Groningen have decided to continue their shelter programs for undocumented migrants without national government funding. Rotterdam, however, will stop its LVV program. For information on how to access local municipality programs, you can consult Helpful Information (HIA).

input: If UM lost access to food/shelter, how could Red Cross programs help them survive?
expected_output: If an undocumented migrant (UM) loses access to food or shelter, the Red Cross can help by referring them to local aid organizations, providing information through their website (https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl), and supporting them via the WhatsApp Helpline. The Red Cross also has food and short-term (10-day) shelter programs, but these are only available through partner organizations. For longer-term shelter, the Red Cross can guide UMs to local BBB or municipality shelter programs, but access depends on specific criteria. Always check local options before making referrals.

input: Which Dutch cities offer BBB shelter programs specifically for undocumented minors, and how are they accessed?
expected_output: The Dutch cities that offer BBB shelter programs specifically for undocumented minors (UM) are Eindhoven, Utrecht, Groningen (screening by Inlia), and Amsterdam. Information about accessing these shelters can be found on the Red Cross Helpful Information website: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ and the LOS website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. For Groningen, screening is done by Inlia: https://www.inlia.nl/nl.

- Amsterdam|Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city. |Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang

When referring undocumented migrants (UM) to medical care providers, keep these key steps and limitations in mind:

**Key Steps:**
- Always clarify that the Red Cross does not provide medical services, only referrals.

- Ensure the UM understands the information and can follow up.

- Not all doctors are familiar with UM rights or may be too busy to help.
- The CAK reimburses 80% of costs for general practitioners and emergency care, but only for contracted providers and only if the UM cannot pay.
- Dental care for adults and some medications are not reimbursed.

input: How can UM access a huisarts or specialized org for medical help, incl. reimbursement options?
expected_output:
Undocumented migrants (UM) have the right to visit a huisarts (family doctor) in the Netherlands, even without residence papers or health insurance. If they have a fixed address, it is best to register with a huisarts for ongoing care. If they are on the street or cannot find a doctor, specialized organizations can help connect them to medical care, often faster and with a network of doctors willing to help UM.

For reimbursement, costs for medical care are covered by the CAK. If a doctor is unsure about this, UM can show them the Red Cross letter explaining their rights and reimbursement process: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

For urgent medical needs after hours, UM should call the huisartsenpost (out-of-hours GP service). In emergencies, hospitals have a legal duty to help and costs can be reimbursed for 80% at the CAK.

Specialized organizations can also assist with dental care, but costs for adults are usually not reimbursed. For more information and contacts, see: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

input: For uninsured individuals, how do fixed address, urgency, and organization networks affect doctor vs. specialized org. referral?
expected_output:
For uninsured individuals:

- **Fixed address:** If someone has a fixed address, it is better to refer them to a doctor (GP) for structural, ongoing care.
- **Urgency:** For urgent medical needs, especially outside office hours, contact the huisartsenpost (GP emergency post) or go to the hospital emergency post, as they have a legal duty to help.
- **Organization networks:** Specialized organizations can quickly help people without health insurance, especially those without a fixed address or who are on the street. These organizations often have networks of doctors willing to see undocumented individuals and can assist in finding a GP.

In summary: Fixed address favors doctor referral; urgency requires emergency services; lack of address or difficulty accessing doctors favors specialized organizations.

input: How can undocumented migrants challenge denial of care by general practitioners in the Netherlands?
expected_output:
Undocumented migrants in the Netherlands have the right to see a doctor, even without residence papers or health insurance. If a general practitioner denies care, migrants can:

1. Clearly explain their rights to the doctor, using the Red Cross letter with information about care for undocumented migrants (available here: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf).
2. Show this letter to the doctor, which explains that costs are reimbursed by the CAK.
3. If still denied, seek help from specialized organizations or contact the Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland for guidance.

Doctors are legally required to provide care, and the CAK reimburses costs for undocumented migrants.

input: Where can undocumented pregnant women access midwife care and shelter during late pregnancy and postpartum?
expected_output: Undocumented pregnant women have the right to see a midwife after three months of pregnancy and can contact a midwife directly without first seeing a doctor.
